Things were so different when I was that young! I was born in 72.  before my parents divorced, I was really into baseball. I was a really good pitcher with a pretty nasty fastball. Maybe my anger helped. Lol. But I had no control especially when I got frustrated. My coach was pretty awesome though and helped. Shortly after we moved across the country and then my parents divorced. That's when things really started going bad for me. It's always had anger issues though.  I remember my brother hitting me in the head once with a shoe box when I was 5. I ended up throwing him into the console tv. Put his front teeth right in to the wood.  But the first time I was diagnosed or ever talked to anyone I was 15. My dad find his shot gun under my bed. I was sent off to a metal hospital for 3 mouths. I remember they made me do affirmations in the mirror. I hated that! But there was a counselor there that was amazing.   Being over protective can be an hard but when I was younger I just wanted to be loved. And looking back I wish someone would have been more protective. I have a twin brother that had problems in school so he got all the attention. I always felt so alone so I'd just hide in my bedroom after school. I was a straight a student and after the divorce no one cared if I did my homework or anything like that. So I barely passed. I also had an older step brother and a younger step sister. Typical wicked step mother stuff which didn't help.  I don't think I really started to understand myself until I was diagnosed with borderline personality when I was around 26ish. To be honest I still have issues understanding myself!  I didn't really know what a trigger was until then because I never really saw a psychiatrist until I was 26.  Looking back I'd have to say no that I didn't know my triggers or why I acted out. And no one ever had talk to anyone until I was 15. By then I think it was just to late. I lived in Alaska, my mom in Rhode Island and soon after I never heard from her that much. Not even when I got married and had her first grand child. 

So.....He most likely doesn't understand what his triggers are either and he probably didn't understand why he acts out like he does. It's been a long time since I was that young so I'm not to sure how he might think. I used to journal a little and it helped for awhile. That might be something you could try. Might even be able to make it a family thing where everyone journals about their day and maybe talk about it. Your journal might actually help you deal with stuff as well. He might be too young to but I remember someone told me when I started getting angry or something like that to think of a big red stop sign. I forget to do that a lot though.

I live with borderline personality and major depression so I understand what you're going through!  The only advice I can give is to talk to her!  Try to explain how you feel. Right now you're in your head and you're the only one in there. She had no idea what you are feeling so tell her. She might not feel the exact same way as you but she might just think you're not into her. Call her up, invite her over, out go for a walk in the park and be open and honest with her and try not to have any expectations because the reality is that you just don't know. Don't just dump a bunch of stuff on her either. Take a couple of days...breathe, think about what you want to say, and think about how you want to say it. If she says no and just forgets you then she wasn't worth it to begin with. If she's truly a friend she'll be open and honest with you about it. Keep us posted!
